title: Rollout sprint lanes cribsheet: milestones, owners, blockers
body:
Purpose:
A compact, action-oriented sprint-lane cribsheet to run customer inference rollouts. Use this as the working single-pane for weekly CS <> SE syncs and QBR prep. Lightweight — copy into a customer-specific tracker and keep one canonical file per account.

How to use: 
- Each row is a milestone lane. Keep owner assignment, RAG, top 3 blockers, and next-step clearly listed.
- Update RAG weekly; escalate persistent red items via the escalation path at the bottom.
- Capture renewal signals (usage, SLA hits, feature adoption) in the Renewal Notes section for QBRs.

Sprint lanes (milestone / owner / due / RAG / blockers -> next action):

1) Kickoff & access / Owner: Maya Chen / Due: 2025-10-15 / RAG: green
   Blockers: none currently.
   Next action: Finalize admin access matrix (CS to confirm list); drop into customer Slack channel.

2) Network & VPC peering / Owner: Omar Singh / Due: 2025-10-29 / RAG: amber
   Blockers: firewall rule approval delayed by customer security team; CIDR overlap question unresolved.
   Next action: Schedule 30-min call with customer infra (owner: Omar) and provide sample env diagram and minimal ACL template.

3) Private deployment validation (smoke tests) / Owner: Jonah Patel / Due: 2025-11-05 / RAG: amber
   Blockers: intermittent GPU node OOM in staging; missing KMS key rotation permissions.
   Next action: SRE run memory-profiling job and share flamegraph by 2025-10-20. CS to collect exact KMS principal list from customer.

4) Model integration & prompts / Owner: Customer (PO: Claire H.) with SE support (Maya) / Due: 2025-11-12 / RAG: yellow
   Blockers: prompt acceptance criteria not finalized; eval harness PR needs review.
   Next action: Align on pass/fail prompt set in workshop (agenda owned by Maya) and merge eval PR: github PR link above.

5) Performance tuning & SLOs / Owner: Jonah Patel / Due: 2025-11-19 / RAG: red
   Blockers: 95th percentile latency target (<=120ms) failing at peak synthetic load; batching config unclear across routes.
   Next action: Run targeted load tests with batching disabled to isolate KV cache issue; coordinate with Serving Runtime (ENG-8765).

6) Compliance review & audit trail / Owner: Omar Singh / Due: 2025-11-26 / RAG: green
   Blockers: policy questions around retention window (customer requests 1 year).
   Next action: Capture retention options and cost delta for 30/90/365 days. Legal to confirm minimal retention requirements.

7) Pilot go-live (limited traffic) / Owner: Claire H. (customer) with CS on-call / Due: 2025-12-03 / RAG: yellow
   Blockers: feature flags for fallback routes not yet implemented in routing policy.
   Next action: Implement canary flag with automatic fallback to hosted model variant; SE to ship flag by 2025-11-25.

Customer-specific blockers (detailed log):
- Firewall approvals pending (ticket with customer security: sec-ticket-1919).
- KMS principals and HSM integration window uncertain — customer needs to confirm procurement timing.
- Intermittent memory pressure observed in staging (heap/KV cache amplification under long-context flows).
- Prompt set not agreed: product and PO need to sign-off (blocking final acceptance criteria).

Escalation path (who to ping):
- Level 1 (CS): Leah Martinez (owner) / Slack: @leah.m / If >48h stale escalate to SE owner.
- Level 2 (SE): Maya Chen / Slack: @maya.c / If blocker still unresolved >72h escalate to ENG on-call and AE.
- Level 3 (Engineering): Jonah Patel (SRE liaison) and Eng on-call; include ENG-8765 in subject.

Renewal signals & QBR prep items to track:
- Usage: tokens/day and percent of routes hitting cached prefixes. Target 60% cache hit before renewal conversation.
- Quality: pass rate on eval harness (regressions < 2% vs baseline).
- Cost: projected per-token cost after batching/quantization recommendations (show delta).
- SLA: current uptime and 95/99 latency percentiles; red if 95th > SLA or >2 incidents in last 30 days.
- Adoption: number of product routes using the deployed model and monthly active end-users.

QBR talking points (quick bullets for CS lead):
- Wins: completed kickoff and admin access; compliance checklist in-progress; initial smoke tests passed baseline.
- Risks: perf tuning stalled (95th latency) and KMS integration timing — these materially affect go-live cadence.
- Ask from customer: request prioritized firewall approvals and KMS procurement timeline.
- Internal ask: AE to surface any contract flexibility for retention window and dedicated capacity if required for perf.

Meeting cadence & artifacts: 
- Weekly sync: 30m, Tue 10am PT (CS+SE+Customer PO). Owner to publish short summary in thread.
- Bi-weekly deep-dive: engineering-led performance review when RAG on perf is amber/red.
- Artifact locations: Confluence playbook (link above), canonical prompt set in repo, load test results in attached google sheet (attach in tracker).

Notes to self (things to follow-up on before next update):
- Confirm exact CIDR ranges with customer and update peering diagram.
- Add example IAM policy snippets for KMS/HSM to the shared folder.
- Prep a short cost-explain slide for QBR showing cost delta of retention vs cache hit improvement.
- Verify if dedicated capacity option would reduce 95th latency below SLA at projected load (quick calc with Eng).

Lightweight change log (what changed since last update):
- 2026-03-01: Updated perf lane to red after last stress run; SRE job scheduled.
- 2026-03-05: Added KMS blocker details and customer procurement note.
- 2026-03-10: Prep notes for QBR added; escalation path clarified.

Files to copy into customer folder when making a canonical tracker:
- This cribsheet (rename with customer prefix).
- access-matrix-template.xlsx
- perf-load-results-YYYY-MM-DD.csv
- prompt-set-v0.3.json

End of cribsheet.
